entries.title: Book V: The Bones and Cartilages
entries.content:
"Dat gaet mi in die beene."
(It took hold of me.)

entries.title: Book V: The Bones and Cartilages
entries.content: Before movement, before sensation, there is structure. The skeleton is no longer symbolic. It becomes measured, proportioned and exact.

entries.title: Book V: The Bones and Cartilages
entries.content: Bones give the body its form—its limits, its proportions, its weight. Cartilage allows flexibility, making movement possible.

entries.title: Book V: The Bones and Cartilages
entries.content: For Vesalius, this begins not in books, but whilst playing outside as a child—bones found, handled, turned over in the hand. In that moment, something takes hold. Not an idea, but a question.

entries.title: Book V: The Bones and Cartilages
entries.content: What begins as fascination becomes inquiry—something that must be understood.
